title: Nine promises
subtitle: Each one tested.
summary: The nine rules every brick and every game on Fizlet keeps, and the test that proves each one.
lead: Most engines assume they own the page. Fizlet is a guest: it runs inside someone else's site, on a phone, next to their code, and it leaves no trace. These nine rules are the whole design. Every brick and every game built on Fizlet keeps them, and each one has a test that fails when it breaks.

items: **One clock.** A kernel test runs several engines and counts one `requestAnimationFrame` between them; another checks the fixed step drops time after `maxSteps` (default 4) instead of spiralling. Details in [the loop](/docs/loop/).

**Bounded.** Pools and the event ring (64 events a frame by default) refuse work at their cap, and the test checks they never grew. `fzlt/fx` refuses particles past its cap (420 by default) and counts them in `fx.dropped`.

**Zero allocation.** One million kernel steps of a busy system cause 0 young-generation GCs on Node 24 (best of three windows; the test fails above 1). Bricks with a hot path have their own allocation tests.
**No layout reads in the step.** `fzlt/debug`'s `guardLayout(engine)` counts layout reads made during a step. The live demo on the [home page](/) shows the count: it stays at 0.

**Change-only writes and Recall.** Browser tests in Chromium write the same value twice and count zero mutations, then `destroy()` and compare the DOM with a snapshot taken before. See [Recall](/docs/recall/).
**Pause by default.** A browser test hides the tab, types in a host field and scrolls the root away, and checks the engine pauses for each reason (`engine.paused`) and runs again after.
**Embed-safe.** A browser test compares every box inside the pad, the match overlay and the launch burst with CSS containment on and off: nothing moves or clips.
**Budgets.** `npm run size` builds every entry, minifies and gzips it, and fails CI over its budget. The numbers are in [budgets](/docs/budgets/).

items.q: Does a game have to keep the contract too?
items.a: Yes. The bricks keep it by construction, and the games on Fizlet are tested against it: they step on typed arrays, write through the ledger and give the page back on Escape.

items.q: Is any rule a frame-rate promise?
items.a: No. The rules bound the work an engine does; real frame time still depends on the page, the fonts and the device. What we measure is in the perf harness, under a 4× CPU throttle.

items.q: Can I break a rule on purpose?
items.a: A change that breaks one needs a test that proves the new rule. That is how the fps cap changed in 0.19.0: it now caps requestAnimationFrame, with a test that counts the calls a second at 60 and 120 Hz.

seo.title: The Fizlet contract: nine tested rules
seo.description: One clock, bounded pools, zero steady-state allocation, change-only writes, pause by default, Recall: the nine rules every Fizlet brick keeps, each tested.
